ruling.recommended_action: Refund $2.56 to the rider's original payment method as the uninformed surge differential; send the driver no notification reminder (RD-7 applies only to route-deviation notification failures, not surge notice).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip's metered distance matched the optimal route exactly — actual 4.0 km against optimal 4.0 km, +0.0 km / −1% [F1], and the billed 4.0 km does not exceed the optimal route [F3] — so there is no route deviation at all under RD-1 (deviation ≤ 1 km → no refund) and RD-2's refund matrix is never engaged. The only live question is the surge, because the multiplier rose from 1.2× at quote [F6] to 1.5× in effect at trip start [F4][F7], which is the increase the trace marks settled under SURGE-2 [F8].

The rider was not notified as SURGE-1 requires: the in-app notice went out at 18:29:30, after the 18:27:00 trip start [F9], and the rider's own complaint says the higher-price message arrived only once she was already in the car. The notice text itself names the new multiplier (1.5×), a revised estimated fare ($19.22) and free cancellation [F9], so it would have satisfied SURGE-1 had it been timely — but timing is the condition, and notice after trip start (and after pickup) fails it. Surge rose and the rider was not notified before or at pickup → refund the differential under SURGE-2.

The differential is computed under SURGE-3 on the mixed-cause basis: (1.5 − 1.2) × $11.29 surgeable subtotal = $3.39 [F8], capped at the $2.56 by which the actual fare ($18.19) exceeds the upfront quote ($15.63) [F6][F7][F8]. The booking fee $1.25 is not surged and stays out of the calculation [F5][F7]. Amount = $2.56.

Because the fare differential is $2.56, under $10, this is a system-final amount on the TH-1/TH-2 path for a fare dispute. The rider's fraud flag (flagged_for_repeated_fare_disputes) [F14] does not change the outcome here — the surge evidence is complete and one-sided — though it raises the confidence threshold to 95% where code applies TH-3; the facts are clear enough that the differential is fixed by the fare records. The driver's statement that the app sets the price and he drove the app's route [F13] is consistent with the records and neither adds nor removes a refund; no traffic or reroute conduct is at issue, so no violation or reminder is recorded. The profile facts (rating, account age, dispute counts) [F14][F15] play no part in the decision.
